title: Samsung could soon charge you for 3 AI features that your friend's Pixel has for free
excerpt: Maybe it's time to drop Galaxy AI for good?
content_html:
Published Nov 26, 2026, 12:15 PM EST

If you’ve ever wondered whether an AI feature on your phone is doing anything useful, Ben Khalesi has probably asked the same question. He has covered AI and Android for Android Police since 2023, with Pixel, Galaxy, Google’s apps, and the rest of the Android ecosystem never far behind. Ben is a lifelong geek with a Bachelor of Information Technology from Macquarie University, where he majored in Data Science and Artificial Intelligence, and he doesn’t stop at reading about AI. He works in AI engineering and automation and even runs his own AI agents on a Raspberry Pi, so when the industry announces something new, he’s the one who wants to know how it works behind the scenes and what can be trusted.

Imagine dictating a text on your Samsung Galaxy phone, only to be told you're out of AI cleanups for the day. That would be strange on a phone you've paid for already.

But what if I told you that, based on a few recent leaks, it might be closer to reality than it sounds?

Samsung appears to be working on its own versions of three AI features that Google gives Pixel owners for free. At the same time, reports say Samsung is testing a paid tier for Galaxy AI.

Neither has been officially announced, and the two may never connect. I'm not one for fearmongering, but I wrote earlier about Samsung possibly charging for Galaxy AI, and here we are.

So allow me my opinions. Let's look at what the leaks show.

Refine Voice Input is Samsung's answer to Rambler

Same job, but is it free?

Rambler launched on the Google Pixel 11 series. Google's November Pixel Drop brought it to the Pixel 10 lineup (10a excluded). It removes filler words like "um" and turns your spoken rambling into polished text.

On Samsung's side, SamMobile found a feature called Refine Voice Input in an internal Samsung Keyboard test build.

Its description says it cleans up "filler words, hesitations, and more." Like Rambler, it reportedly shows your text only after you finish speaking.

The feature has since shown up in One UI 9.5 beta firmware, and according to a breakdown by leaker Ice Universe, it switches off when you limit Galaxy AI to on-device processing. That hints that it relies on the cloud.

That leaves one big question. Will Refine Voice Input be a free keyboard upgrade, or will it count against a Galaxy AI usage limit?

Memory is Samsung's take on Pixel Screenshots

Samsung seems to be casting an even wider net

SamMobile reports that Samsung is working on a standalone Galaxy AI app called Memory, expected to debut with One UI 9.5.

It takes in screenshots, links, text, voice notes, and content you import from other apps.

Memory then uses AI to write titles and summaries, add tags, and group related items into collections. It can even recover the original webpage link from a screenshot.

That's Pixel Screenshots territory. Google's version comes built into the Pixel 9 series and later, runs on on-device AI, and doesn't need a subscription.

The more telling detail is where Memory does its processing. According to leaks, it sends your saves to the cloud first and only processes them on the device when the cloud isn't available.

That makes Memory a good test of Samsung's promise. Samsung says core Galaxy AI features will stay free, but a cloud-powered app that summarizes everything you save sounds a lot like the "advanced" tools it says could become paid.

Looks like another clone, but is there AI involved?

The clue is a My Custom Widget option that leaker Fahad Ali Javed spotted in an early One UI 9.5 build back in August.

His screenshot shows a widget split into two sections. One side has a Calendar card for a dinner plan. The other has buttons to view or share it. There is also a hard-to-miss title saying "Make your own widget."

What nobody knows yet is how you'd make one. The leak doesn't show a prompt box or any AI step, so there's no proof Samsung has built a prompt-driven widget generator.

Still, my instinct says it is one. Samsung isn't the type to trail behind Google for long.

But for now, Google is much further ahead. It announced Create My Widget in May and opened a Play Store beta for the Pixel 10 and Pixel 11 series in November.

Galaxy AI Premium is still a test

The leaked prices may not be final

SammyGuru reports that Samsung is testing Galaxy AI Premium through an opt-in early-access program. Strings in the app list a Max plan at $5 a month or $48 a year.

Max reportedly gives you four times the usage of the free plan, plus three new features called Gen Video, Bixby Action, and Daily Briefing.

The free plan keeps today's Galaxy AI tools, but reports say those tools will come with usage limits. Again, none of this is final.

Samsung hasn't announced the plan, and there's no guarantee the leaked prices will stick. What Samsung has confirmed is the broader idea.

Samsung has previously said its core Galaxy AI features will stay free, while certain advanced capabilities or new services may become paid options.

On paper, a capped feature still counts as free, so Samsung could keep that promise and still ration what you get.

Samsung also decides what counts as "core" and what counts as "advanced," and nothing stops that line from moving with each One UI update.

Samsung's biggest rival is Google's free AI

There's already some skepticism on r/Android. Some commenters say they'll stick with Gemini as their assistant and won't pay for Galaxy AI.

It's still too early for a backlash, but it does show Samsung's problem. People will weigh any price against the tools that already work for free on their phones or a Pixel.

It doesn't help that Google says its Gemini Intelligence features are coming to the Samsung Galaxy S26 series and the company's latest foldables.

If Rambler is among them, some Galaxy owners could end up with Google's free version and Samsung's possibly capped one on the same phone.

I'm fine with paying a premium for a feature after it earns it. However, everyday tasks with a usage limit are where I draw the line. If that happens, sorry, Samsung, but I'm with the Reddit crowd.
